newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rojo sees need for caution on CPI news-Efe.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rojo sees need for caution on CPI news-Efe.

text.p: The Bank of Spain dismissed as groundless on Tuesday a local news report purporting to quote from a speech central bank governor Luis Angel Rojo is to deliver in Congress on Wednesday.

The report carried by state news agency Efe, which said it had obtained a copy of Rojo's speech, quoted him as calling for moderation on salaries and pushing for structural reforms to make the Spanish economy more efficient.

Rojo was reported as warning that excessive increases in labour costs this year could damage the downward trend of inflation and could make it necessary to "take the most extreme caution" in evaluating the drop in consumer prices.
He said that, although July's consumer prices rate was satisfactory, it was still 1.3 points higher than the average of the three European countries with a smaller inflation rate.
The central bank governor was leaning toward a "more decided advance" in the structural reforms that could make the Spanish economy more flexible and efficient.
The Bank of Spain said the Efe report was about a speech known only to Rojo and his secretary and that was subject to change up until the time of the presentation.

The report quoted Rojo as saying the reactivation of the 1996 economy supported a "modest recovery in private consumption, with slight improvement in capital goods investment and export impetus and above all centred on food, compensating for listlessness in the construction sector."
